An independent school providing innovative specialist education for autistic young people.
Welcome to Hambrook School
Hambrook School is an independent special school for students aged 5-18.
Located in the town of Burgess Hill, West Sussex, our dedicated and professional team strive to ensure our children are safe, engage in their learning while having fun.
Our Vision
We use a range of best practice strategies and interventions to deliver highly individualised learning opportunities for our pupils.
Our Values
The school places particular emphasis on collaboration.This way our students move on comfortably to engage with education and reach their full potential.
Our Aims
We are ambitious about what each of our pupils can achieve, regardless of their starting point, and take pride in recording, sharing and celebrating the progress they each make as individuals.
© Outcomes First Group 2026

Home Parents and Carers Referrals and admissions
Referrals and admissions
Admissions:
Hambrook School accepts referrals from parents and local authorities. We encourage parents to engage in a dialogue with their child’s current school SENCo and/or local authority in the first instance. Typically, we receive referrals from local authorities once an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP) has been agreed.
Upon receiving a referral, leaders will review the paperwork to see if the school is likely to meet the child/young persons needs. If leaders feel that needs could be met, an initial offer to assess the child/young person is made. All offers to assess are directed to the local authority in the first instance.
Following an assessment, which may take place at the child or young persons home and/or current school, the team will confirm if Hambrook School can meet the their needs. If the assessment team feel that needs can be met, a visit to the school will be offered. The nature and duration of this visit will be tailored to the needs of each child/young person.
At the end of this process, an offer letter is sent to the local authority with starting dates and fees. Within the first 12 weeks of the child starting at the school, we will arrange for a post admission review to be held. At this meeting, the placement will be discussed and any amendments to the provision agreed with parents/carers and the local authority.
Hambrook School accepts referrals for children and young people who are:
If you’d like to make a referral or you simply want to know more, please don’t hesitate to get in touch.
© Outcomes First Group 2026

Home Parents and Carers
Parents & Carers
The parents and carers of the children and young people we educate and care for are so important, and we take care to give them all the expert ongoing support they need at every stage of their partnership with us.
From the moment they make their first enquiry and right through the child or young person’s time in one of our schools or residential homes, we’re there for them with tailored advice and support.
Tune in to Autism Unpacked, where we’re navigating SEN together through honest conversations, expert insight, lived experience and practical advice.
We’re joined by professionals from education and therapy, alongside parents, carers and people with lived experience, to share practical insights, explore the topics that matter and help families and those supporting children and young people feel better informed.
© Outcomes First Group 2026

Curriculum
Our individually tailored curriculum covers all National Curriculum subjects in imaginative and flexible ways.
Our ultimate aim at Hambrook School is to prepare our students for life in modern Britain, and whatever the next stage of their journey may be, whether that is employment, further education, or something else entirely.
In addition, we deliver an autism-specific curriculum based on the following eight areas of the Autism Education Trust’s Pupil Progression Framework:
Across the curriculum, we incorporate work on pupils’ spiritual, moral, social and cultural development, as well as encouraging their understanding of core British values.

Home Our Approach Clinical Team
Clinical Therapy
At Hambrook, our Clinical Team plays an important role in supporting your child’s health and wellbeing, learning, and development.
The Hambrook school team includes a:
Working together, we help young people with their communication, sensory differences, emotional regulation, and growing independence.
We follow the OFG neurodiversity affirming strategy Ask, Accept, Develop (AAD), which recognises and celebrates each young person’s unique strengths and supports development of self-advocacy and independence. We also use the 3 C’s approach (connect, co-regulate, and co-reflect) which helps staff understand how past experiences, including trauma, may influence behaviour. This strategy encourages calm, thoughtful support and helps build strong, trusting relationships with our pupils.
At the heart of our approach is the OFG clinical pyramid, which provides differentiated levels of therapeutic support within the specialist school setting. This allows us to match our support to the strengths, differences, and needs of each pupil. Therapeutic support is often embedded into the day allowing individuals to development and generalise skills learnt within the school environment. Where a therapeutic intervention is prescribed on a pupils EHCP, the Clinical team will assess, review and support those needs, either providing direct therapy where recommended or programmes to be carried out in a classroom environment.
As part of Outcomes First Group’s ‘ALL’ level of support, the Clinical team work collaboratively with education teams to offer integrated whole-school input to meet the needs of all pupils. This includes:
Our clinical team follows a high-quality, consistent approach that is tailored to the needs of each individual. We are committed to inclusion, equality, and diversity, and we work holistically to support all areas of a young person’s development. We are based on site at Hambrook school so we can collaborate closely with school staff and families, sharing information appropriately, and always follow professional and regulatory standards, so you can feel confident in the care your child receives.
If you would like to know more information about our clinical pyramid and our levels of provision, please click the link below.

Home About Us Meet Our Team
Meet our team
Welcome to Hambrook School from the Headteacher.
I am very excited to be part of this amazing, fun and caring school where the students are at the heart of everything we do.
Set in the former Adult Education Centre in Burgess Hill we are continuing a legacy of learning by preparing the next generation of children and young adults to feel confident and independent in their own lives.
We work hard to provide a variety of bespoke learning opportunities in smaller class environments catered to the student’s individual needs.
We do this with the support of specialist practitioners including teachers, clinicians, support staff, outside agencies, colleges and other education providers with one aim in mind:
Provide a safe and enjoyable learning experience eradicating learnt helplessness while empowering children and young adults to be Safe, Enjoy their Learning and Have Fun so that they can be confident, independent citizens in the world.
The curriculum here is robust, engaging and targeted. We want students to embrace a hands-on approach to learning, letting them investigate and experience activities and curricula that will inspire them to find out more.
We will guide and advocate achievement by nurturing aspirational goals, establish a love of reading and discovery that will enhance their learning journey. We believe that our students deserve the best as they start their own education expedition with us and we will work in partnership with parents, carers and members of our local communities to achieve that goal.
Come and visit us and find out what we can do for you.
Emile Etheridge – Headteacher & DDSL
All of our staff are proud to be a team in our school. We celebrate that we are all individuals. Read our bios to find out more about us here.

Home About Us Proprietor
Proprietor
Hambrook School is operated by P Bloom Ltd.
Hambrook School is owned by Options Autism (7) Ltd and is a fully owned subsidiary of P. Bloom Ltd, which is part of Outcomes First Group, a provider of children’s services in the UK.
Hambrook School has its own dedicated management team, under the leadership of Emile Etheridge, Headteacher. Oversight of school management is provided by the Regional Director for Options Autism, Jason Pearn, responsible to the Operations Director, Richard Adams-Murgatroyd, and Chief Operating Officer, Richard Power.
Richard Power also acts as the registered Proprietor Chairperson for P. Bloom Ltd.
The management team is complemented by Group support functions covering Quality and Compliance, Admissions and Marketing, Human Resources, Finance and IT. Key decisions are referred to Outcomes First Group’s Board of Directors, consisting of Outcomes First Group CEO, Richard Power and CFO, Jean-Luc Janet, together with an independent Chairman and three Non-Executive Directors.
In addition, the Group continues its robust governance through local governing committees, a national education performance board, chaired by the Operations Director and an independent Safeguarding and Quality Committee with three independent members. These governance groups meet every term.

Hambrook’s Three School Rules
